title: Medicines designed from a confirmed human disease mechanism

concept.text: The innovation is a prospective method for designing psychiatric medicines from a confirmed human disease mechanism. Researchers would identify a disease-relevant biological abnormality, develop a drug or biological treatment intended to correct it, and predict which patients should benefit before the treatment’s efficacy is known. Clinical testing would then examine whether correcting that abnormality produces the predicted improvement. The abnormality need not be a single mutation or visible structural lesion; it could be a defined molecular or biological process.

Conceptual synthesis: the defining achievement would be a tested chain connecting human disease biology, an intervention designed around that biology, and the predicted clinical response. A drug’s action at a receptor, a biomarker that predicts response, or an explanation developed after an unexpected clinical success would each provide useful evidence, but none alone would establish this complete design capability. PSY-05 concerns the method for creating treatments; it does not require that the resulting medicine cure an illness or permanently change its course.

significance.text: A reliable route from human disease mechanism to treatment would substantially change psychiatric drug development. Howes and Baxter’s 2023 editorial describes a history in which clinical observation and empirical discovery were followed by efforts to develop related compounds. A prospectively validated mechanism could instead give investigators a reason to build a particular intervention and a biological basis for choosing the patients most likely to benefit.

Conditional synthesis: the immediate achievement would be one mechanistically justified treatment, followed by an independently confirmed second prediction from the same framework. That would demonstrate repeatability within the tested framework. It could support more informative patient selection, clearer interpretation of treatment failures, and subsequent treatment hypotheses. Two successes would not guarantee that the framework can generate further medicines or generalize across psychiatric disorders.

The potential for disease modification is consequential but separate. Pawlak and colleagues’ review discusses interventions affecting synaptic pruning as possible ways to alter disease trajectories, while emphasizing biological heterogeneity and the need for further validation. A medicine designed from a causal mechanism might still provide benefit only while it is taken. Claims of prevention, durable course change, or lasting recovery would require their own evidence.

Analogy and scope: targeting a known causal abnormality offers a useful comparison with mechanism-guided treatment elsewhere in medicine. The supplied material does not establish the research notes’ specific historical claim about when oncology acquired this method. Nor does the analogy imply that psychiatric disorders generally have a single actionable lesion. Success in one biologically defined subgroup could be revolutionary without making every disorder curable or replacing all symptom-directed treatment.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central scientific barrier is connecting molecular processes to psychiatric symptoms strongly enough to guide intervention. Howes and Baxter identify this incomplete understanding as an obstacle to finding new drug targets. A biological association must be developed into an explanation of how the process contributes to illness and why changing it should improve a specified clinical outcome.

Clinical heterogeneity creates a second barrier: patients sharing a diagnosis may have different underlying mechanisms. The synaptic-neuroscience review gives a concrete example in schizophrenia, noting that excessive pruning or inflammatory markers are not present in every patient and that pruning-directed interventions might benefit only particular subgroups. Mechanism-guided development therefore needs a dependable way to identify the relevant biology in individual patients, rather than relying solely on a syndromic diagnosis.

Engineering and inference synthesis: investigators must turn the proposed mechanism into a measurable patient abnormality, an intervention that reaches and changes the intended target, and a trial capable of testing the predicted clinical consequence. Target engagement is necessary evidence but does not itself prove that the abnormality causes symptoms. Likewise, a biomarker can predict response without identifying the process the medicine corrects. The missing capability is the integration of these elements into a convincing prospective causal account.

The supplied evidence documents these barriers and motivates the proposed capability. It does not establish that every part of psychiatry still lacks such a capability as of November 1, 2026. Establishing field-wide absence would require a sufficiently current and comprehensive assessment that is not present in the supplied record.

current_state.text: Howes and Baxter’s 2023 editorial reports 12 new FDA-approved psychiatric drugs during 2011–2021, compared with 50 in neurology and 135 in oncology, and two psychiatric first-in-class designations during 2015–2021. These are dated counts reported by the editorial; the supplied review did not independently audit the underlying counting method. The editorial also documents the history of empirical discovery and the unresolved link between molecular processes and symptoms. It does not quantify the present-day dominance of particular drug classes.

On September 26, 2024, the FDA approved Cobenfy for treatment of schizophrenia in adults, describing it as the first approved schizophrenia antipsychotic targeting cholinergic rather than dopamine receptors. The FDA release reports two five-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter studies in adults selected using DSM-5 schizophrenia criteria. Efficacy was assessed through symptom improvement using the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale. This establishes a new receptor approach with short-term symptomatic efficacy; those studies do not establish correction of a confirmed disease abnormality or durable disease modification.

Cobenfy’s approval indication should not be described as explicitly limited to acute treatment merely because the reported efficacy trials lasted five weeks. The supplied FDA document is a complete press release, rather than a full trial report or a comprehensive account of the drug’s development. It supports the distinction between receptor novelty and the prospective disease-mechanism design capability proposed here, while leaving broader developmental claims unestablished.

Pawlak and colleagues’ review, published October 15, 2025, discusses complement component 4A, or C4A, as an implicated pathway and reports that no clinical trials directly target C4A modulation. This is an attributed review statement, not an independently verified trial-registry finding through November 2026. The supplied assessment notes that its attached reference is a 2014 genetic-loci paper rather than a contemporary trial inventory. C4A remains a relevant mechanistic lead in this account, but the supplied evidence does not establish its ranking as the clearest molecular clue from common variation.

The retained review copy is marked corrected September 30, 2026; the separate correction text was not supplied, so its effect on the relevant claims is unresolved. The supplied assessment relied on a complete retained PDF for the textual passages because the retained HTML extraction was truncated in its references. These limitations affect confidence in the interpretation and freshness of the trial-absence statement; they do not establish that the statement is false.

The available record therefore supports documented mechanistic barriers, an approved receptor innovation, and an active biological research direction. It does not verify the research notes’ exact schizophrenia-associated-loci count, their attribution to Ghaemi, or their categorical assertion that no approved psychiatric medicine meets the proposed design standard. No bounded freshness-search entries were supplied, so the innovation’s field-wide achievement status as of November 1, 2026 remains open.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: before efficacy results are known, investigators would publish the human disease mechanism, the predicted clinical effect, and a validated method for identifying the relevant patient subset. They would also specify why the intervention should correct the abnormality and which measurements would test that prediction. These are proposed criteria for PSY-05, not an established consensus standard.
completion_criteria.label: Publish mechanism, predicted benefit, and validated patient selection before efficacy

completion_criteria.text: An adequately controlled trial would demonstrate clinically meaningful benefit in the prespecified subset and directly test the predicted treatment-by-subset difference. Finding a statistically significant effect in one subgroup and a nonsignificant effect in another would not by itself establish differential benefit. If the theory predicts little or no benefit outside the subset, estimates must be precise enough to assess that prediction; a null result alone cannot demonstrate absence of benefit.
completion_criteria.label: Meaningful benefit and predicted treatment-by-subset difference in controlled trial

completion_criteria.text: Target-engagement and mechanistic measurements would support the sequence from intervention to biological correction to clinical improvement. The demonstration should address whether the subset marker identifies the proposed causal process or merely correlates with treatment response. An effective medicine with a plausible retrospective explanation would remain valuable, but would not by itself satisfy this prospective design test.
completion_criteria.label: Measurements support biological correction mediating treatment’s predicted clinical benefit

completion_criteria.text: A second prediction generated by the same framework would then be specified in advance and tested independently. Replication should establish that the patient-selection measurement and clinical result are reproducible. The second test should add predictive content rather than simply redescribe the first success. Finite successful tests would establish demonstrated breadth within the tested populations, mechanisms, and outcomes, rather than literal universality.
completion_criteria.label: Independent second prediction confirms reproducible patient selection and clinical results

completion_criteria.text: Practical boundaries would be reported explicitly: who can be identified reliably, what benefit is achieved, how long it lasts, and what harms or delivery constraints accompany it. A claim of disease modification would require evidence of changed illness course beyond the symptomatic efficacy needed to demonstrate the design method. Prevention, sustained remission, and durable recovery would each need suitable follow-up and separate outcome definitions.
completion_criteria.label: Report practical limits of patient identification and treatment outcomes

related_concepts.text: Roster synthesis — PSY-01, “Mechanism-defined diseases in place of the major syndromes,” concerns how illnesses are classified. It could supply the biological patient groups needed for PSY-05, while PSY-05 asks whether those mechanisms can prospectively guide successful medicine design. PSY-06, “A clinical instrument that reads an individual’s psychiatric state,” could provide patient-selection or response measurements, but measuring a state does not establish its cause or identify a corrective treatment.

Roster synthesis — PSY-02, “A treatment that changes the course of schizophrenia,” and PSY-03, “Ending the relapsing course of severe mood disorders,” define illness-course outcomes. A medicine developed through PSY-05 could contribute to either, but mechanism-guided design does not itself demonstrate a changed course. PSY-04, “Primary prevention that lowers incidence of a major disorder,” similarly requires evidence of reduced new illness. Each remains a distinct achievement even if a single intervention eventually satisfies more than one concept.

Roster synthesis — PSY-07, “Reliable causal control of a core symptom by a defined circuit,” concerns causal intervention at the circuit level. It could strengthen the bridge from biology to symptoms needed for PSY-05, but circuit control alone does not demonstrate a medicine designed to correct a confirmed disease mechanism. PSY-10, “Reopening plasticity that can repair an established psychiatric deficit,” concerns a specific repair capability; a plasticity-directed medicine would overlap with PSY-05 only if its design and prospective clinical validation met the mechanism-based criteria.

Roster synthesis — PSY-08, “Selective and durable modification of a pathological memory,” defines a particular lasting therapeutic effect. PSY-11, “Prevention of post-traumatic stress disorder by blocking consolidation,” defines a preventive intervention with a specific timing and biological rationale. Either could involve mechanism-guided medicines, but selective memory modification and prevention of PTSD require evidence beyond demonstrating the PSY-05 design method.

Roster synthesis — PSY-09, “A time-limited reset of severe addiction,” requires a durable outcome after a bounded intervention; a mechanism-designed medicine could instead require ongoing treatment. PSY-12, “A session-level amplifier that lets brief psychotherapy match a full course,” concerns increased psychotherapy efficiency. Such an amplifier could be developed through PSY-05, while equivalence to a full course would remain a separate clinical demonstration. These entries retain their distinct outcome requirements.

unresolved_issues: Whether an approved or otherwise convincingly demonstrated psychiatric treatment already meets the proposed PSY-05 criteria as of November 1, 2026; the supplied freshness-search record is empty.
What the September 30, 2026 correction to the Pawlak review changed, and whether it affects the C4A discussion or trial-absence statement.
Whether a contemporary trial inventory confirms the review’s statement that no trials directly target C4A modulation.
The research notes’ Ghaemi attribution, exact schizophrenia-associated-loci count, and comparative ranking of C4A remain unverified in the supplied evidence.

The proposed demonstration still requires operational definitions of a confirmed human mechanism, adequate mechanistic measurement, a clinically meaningful effect, and an independently informative second prediction.
No substantive review recommendation was rejected; unsupported assertions were qualified or replaced with bounded statements rather than used to dismiss the concept.

brief.title: Mental health medicines designed around disease causes
possible: People with a psychiatric illness could receive a medicine designed to correct a biological problem contributing to their symptoms. Before testing whether it works, researchers would predict who should benefit and why, then test whether correcting that problem produces the expected improvement.
why: Researchers could choose which medicines to build from an understanding of human illness. Biological tests could help identify the patients most likely to benefit and make treatment failures easier to explain.

An independently confirmed second prediction would show that the approach can work repeatedly within the biology and patient groups tested. That would give researchers a firmer basis for developing further treatments.

sources.showed: Cobenfy reduced schizophrenia symptoms compared with an inactive substitute. It targets a different set of receptors, the cell proteins drugs bind to, from earlier approved schizophrenia medicines.
sources.quote: In both studies, the participants who received Cobenfy experienced a meaningful reduction in symptoms from baseline to Week 5
sources.cited_for: A medicine acting through different receptors can improve schizophrenia symptoms.
sources.not_established: The trials do not establish that correcting a confirmed biological cause produced the improvement.

sources.who: Oliver D Howes and Luke Baxter
sources.showed: Their editorial describes how psychiatric drug development has relied on clinical observations and trials, while links between biological processes and symptoms remain poorly understood.
sources.quote: Much psychiatric drug development has been based on astute clinical observation and empirical studies, followed by extensive efforts to then develop related compounds.
sources.cited_for: Understanding how biological processes produce symptoms is a central barrier to designing treatments around disease causes.
sources.not_established: The editorial does not demonstrate a treatment whose biological correction produces a clinical benefit predicted in advance.

sources.showed: Their review examines excessive pruning, the removal of connections between brain cells. Antibiotic trials remain inconclusive despite hints of benefit in studies looking back at patient records.
sources.quote: While retrospective studies suggest minocycline or doxycycline may reduce psychosis risk, randomized trials remain inconclusive.
sources.cited_for: Excessive pruning offers a possible treatment target, but the relevant biology differs between patients.
sources.not_established: The review does not establish that correcting excessive pruning produces the predicted clinical benefit in a reliably identified patient group.

shown: Bristol-Myers Squibb’s Cobenfy has demonstrated symptom relief through a different receptor approach. Pawlak and colleagues describe excessive pruning as a possible biological target in schizophrenia. These advances provide treatment options and research leads.
missing: A confirmed link between a measurable biological abnormality and the symptoms a treatment is intended to improve is needed.
A dependable test must identify which patients have the relevant biological problem.
A trial must connect correction of that problem to the clinical improvement predicted before testing.
An independent test must confirm a further prediction from the same framework.

milestones.label: The biological explanation and patient test are published before results
milestones.explanation: Researchers would have to publish the disease process, predicted benefit, validated patient test and planned checks of biological correction before efficacy results. This would make the prediction testable.

milestones.label: A controlled trial confirms the predicted differences between patient groups
milestones.explanation: A controlled trial would have to show meaningful benefit and directly test the predicted difference between patient groups with sufficient precision. This would test whether patient selection works.

milestones.label: Biological correction explains the predicted clinical benefit
milestones.explanation: Measurements would have to support biological correction as the cause of the predicted clinical improvement. This would distinguish correcting a disease process from merely predicting who responds.

milestones.label: An independent test confirms a further prediction
milestones.explanation: An independent test would have to confirm a further prediction from the same framework, reproducing patient selection and clinical results. This would establish repeatability beyond the initial success.

milestones.label: The practical limits of treatment are reported
milestones.explanation: Results would have to report who can be identified reliably, benefits, duration, harms and delivery constraints. This would define practical use, with separate evidence needed for lasting changes to illness.

uncertain: It remains open whether an existing psychiatric treatment already meets the complete standard.
What would count as a confirmed disease process and convincing evidence that correcting it causes improvement?
How much new predictive content would an independent test need to establish repeatability?

page.title: Mechanism-based psychiatric drug development
page.definition: Psychiatric medicines are designed or selected to correct a biological process shown to contribute causally to human illness. Before efficacy testing, a measure of that process identifies patients expected to benefit; controlled studies establish the predicted clinical benefit and its link to biological correction.

goal.need: Howes and Baxter report 12 new psychiatric drugs approved by the FDA during 2011–2021, compared with 135 in oncology. They also report the first-in-class counts below. Their proposed route forward connects human disease biology to target discovery, patient selection and measurement of drug effects.

figures.note: Historical editorial counts. First-in-class status does not establish correction of a causal disease mechanism.

statements.context: The roadmap identifies this as a consequence of stratifying patients into biologically homogeneous populations.

brexanolone was developed by design—a design centered around a molecule called allopregnanolone

completion.title: A prospective human study validates a psychiatric medicine designed to correct a causal disease mechanism.
completion.criterion: A psychiatric medicine is designed or selected from human evidence that a measurable biological abnormality contributes causally to illness. Patients and the expected clinical response are specified from that mechanism before efficacy is known. Controlled human testing demonstrates the predicted benefit, correction of the abnormality and evidence that this correction causes the benefit, with competing explanations such as off-target action addressed. A treatment-response correlation alone does not satisfy the causal test.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; operational criterion informed by NIMH experimental therapeutics and the ECNP and ACNP roadmaps.
completion.basis: Searches of NIMH trial criteria, FDA schizophrenia-approval materials, and the ECNP and ACNP roadmaps found no test for the complete causal design chain. NIMH's positive-result rule combines benefit and target change without establishing disease causation. Brexanolone is a design-led precedent, but its phase 3 trials selected women by postpartum depression and symptom severity, not a measured causal abnormality. The Atlas test retains the missing prospective causal link.

milestones.title: A psychiatric drug candidate engages its target in a preclinical system with a pharmacodynamic readout.
milestones.criterion: Establish a pharmacodynamic biomarker, a measurable biological response to a drug, in a preclinical system; relate downstream readouts to molecular target engagement. The NAMHC workgroup supplies no universal numerical cutoff. In a 2015 rat study, LY2456302 saturated κ-opioid receptors at oral doses of 3–300 mg/kg, measured 60 minutes after dosing, with four rats per dose; pupil responses assessed unwanted activity at another opioid receptor.
milestones.set_by: National Advisory Mental Health Council Workgroup on Drug Development, 2020 report, section IV; recommendation concerning preclinical pharmacodynamic biomarkers.
milestones.threshold_quote: it is critical to establish it in preclinical systems

milestones.title: A psychiatric drug candidate engages its brain target at tolerated doses in people.
milestones.criterion: Human dose-ranging demonstrates brain target engagement, characterizes exposure and pharmacological effects, and establishes tolerability for further testing. NIMH specifies no universal occupancy cutoff. In a 2016 report, LY2456302 was given to 13 healthy adults; 12 contributed occupancy data. At 10 mg orally, mean κ-opioid receptor occupancy was 94% at 2.5 hours and 72% at 24 hours (n=3). No serious adverse events occurred.
milestones.set_by: National Institute of Mental Health, PAR-25-180, first-in-human and early-stage pharmacological studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: objectively and dose dependently assess target engagement in the central nervous system (CNS), along with safety and tolerability.

milestones.title: A psychiatric drug's target engagement is linked to symptom or functional improvement in patients.
milestones.criterion: Replicate target engagement and establish safety, tolerability and an association between target change and symptom/function change in patients. NIMH specifies no universal numerical cutoff. FAST-MAS (2020) randomized 89 adults with reduced pleasure and mood/anxiety disorders to JNJ-67953964 10 mg/day (45) or placebo (44) for 8 weeks. The primary brain-activation endpoint favoured drug (g=0.58; one-sided p=0.0095); activation change correlated with pleasure-scale change (r=0.20; p<0.05).
milestones.set_by: National Institute of Mental Health, PAR-25-184, R33 phase and its decision about further development.
milestones.threshold_quote: including evidence of safety, tolerability, altered CNS physiology, and strength of the association between target engagement and change in symptoms/function.

milestones.title: A psychiatric drug confirms clinical superiority and target engagement in a fully powered patient trial.
milestones.criterion: A fully powered controlled trial demonstrates clinical superiority, replicates target engagement and tests whether target change accounts for benefit. VENTURA-1's sponsor summary dated 12 September 2025 reports 511 treated participants. In 337 adults with moderate-to-severe loss of pleasure, 6-week Montgomery–Åsberg Depression Rating Scale scores fell 11.7 points with aticaprant 10 mg plus antidepressant (n=170) and 10.7 with placebo plus antidepressant (n=167). The sponsor reported no meaningful difference. These results are not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: National Institute of Mental Health, PAR-25-179, confirmatory efficacy studies; pharmacological support primarily concerns medicines already approved for another indication.
milestones.threshold_quote: replicate these target engagement and validation findings in a fully powered, confirmatory efficacy study

not_found: A comprehensive assessment of existing psychiatric medicines against the full causal and prospective completion test was not found.
